claims.claim: Reviewers mention difficulty with the tutorial, noting issues such as getting stuck on horseback lancing challenges or finding the instructions tedious and unhelpful for learning core mechanics.

citations.review_text:
The combat is glorious and the most fulfilling from any game I've ever played. It’s like rock-paper-scissors mixed with "two for flinching," at least on the surface. The interplay of the various elements and mechanics is glorious, and it feels rewarding to master.

But you probably won't master them. I've been playing this game effectively since its release and I can tell you this: levels 0–100 are generally considered the learning curve just to grasp the basics. The Tutorial is hot garbage that doesn't teach you any of the true essentials, assuming a new player even plays it. There’s very little reason to do so beyond the gold bonus you receive for completion.

If you want to learn the basics, you need someone to teach you. Things like swing manipulation, accels, drags, chambers, or even ripostes are misunderstood by some players.

Dueling and team fighting require entirely different skill sets. Being good at one will not automatically make you good at the other.

The Devs don't know how to balance team skill either. They ought to take the average level of every player on the server and then try to create two teams with an approximate combination of skill. This is why only 26 people were on the server at a time when the game was free.

Players have complained about "team stacking for ages," but it's a myth. At the time of writing, team selection has been disabled. Teams get crushed more thoroughly now than they ever have before. This shows us that the issue wasn't that good players would join the same team to win games previously. Instead, simply using autoselect at the start without any true balancing mechanism would lead to this situation. Now, as a level 218 player, I can't even swap to the losing team to try and balance things myself.

The Devs don't play their own game. The Devs don't moderate their own community. They don't push content at anything close to a reasonable speed, and if something's broken, expect at least 6 months of sitting on the busted issue …

-------The Tutorial-------
The first 5-min of tutorial was awesome. 
It taught you how to attack, parry and do combos.
And the bow and arrows, all felt easy peasy.  

However, the Couched Attack on Horseback, I stuck there for at least 15-min.
A small range where you constantly hitting invisible walls while charging the speed up. It requires you to ride fast and gives you a small tiny area. The stamina is not depleted and hit four dummies with a couched lance on horseback is not fun at all - somehow I managed 3/4 after numerous tries, and the last one is such a pain. 

The F for Couch while horse riding probably only works 1 out of 100 times. 
Google it and found a Reddit post from 6 years ago, complaining about the couching. 

This whole lancing on the horseback thing is just bad.
The horse is so unhinged, which makes you feel out of control. 
I was about to uninstall this game and unlocked the last one, and finished the tutorial. 

-------The Game-------
Joined a random match with lots of bots.
Landed to the world naked with no weapons.
Hide in the corner and every enemy is lethal.

Collected a few coins and points after a few waves.
Spent them on basic clothing items and weapons.
Revived a few allies.

Finally got a closer look of the enemies, died in the middle of fire.
Chaotic bots running around...bought myself a bow. 
Guess what, the headshot damage was only 15 for newbies.
Armor upgrades, unlock new weapons and skill trees, it's just pure grinding. 

I guess after playing NewWorld and other MMOs, this one just felt outdated, not visually pleasing and unbalanced.
For the 85% off sale, sure you can have some fun with it. The server was quiet and bots are endless. 

In between of each waves, there are 20 seconds countdown. 
Endless loops.
And that 20 seconds made me think, time to quit the game.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a cooperative wave-based mode where players defend against enemy hordes.

citations.review_text:
[Played this while it was free for a few days.]

Of all the games of this type, beginning with Mount & Blade, this one plays the worst. 

There's an artificial lag put onto attacks in all of them, so that opponents can have an actual chance to see that attacks are coming and where from. Makes parrying a viable option. Yet, in all the other titles it doesn't seem as bad as here. Combined with minimal defensive options, a lack of useful hit feedback and weapons not having the reach that visuals seem to imply, combat isn't as fun as the videos want to make you believe.

There's at least one positive, though. Mordhau has a coop-only mode, where you defend your position against waves of increasing enemy hordes. It's not fleshed out enough to provide long lasting fun before becoming repetitive. But at least you can level and customize your character with skill points and money between waves. There's lots of weapons and armor to pick from. The existence of this mode makes it much easier to learn combat than by fighting against players with far superior skill levels.

Maybe recommendable while on sale. It's not horrible and might give enough entertainment for at least a few hours. Just know that there are better games of this kind.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game features a steep learning curve and high skill gap for newer players facing veteran opponents.

citations.review_text: i seen better melee combat in a school cafeteria

It's honestly more fun against bots than people.

Edit: Changed my mind, bots are BS. The game is fun, but has a very steep learning curve that just puts you off it.

When it's good, it's some of the most fun melee combat out there 100%, but unfortunately, getting to those moments means wading through a brutal learning curve, sweaty veterans, and enough chaos to make improvement feel optional.

MORDHAU is actually a really good game, and I can see why people loved it when it first came out back in April 2019. The combat is fun, the weapons feel good, and the whole medieval chaos thing is still really cool.
The problem is trying to get into it now. Most of the people still playing are level 200 to 300 with thousands of hours, usually like 3k to 5k, and they already know every weird combo and animation trick in the game. A lot of it does not even feel like normal combat anymore. It feels like they are abusing stuff that was never really meant to be used that way.
It would not be so bad if the community was chill, but a lot of the high-level players are toxic too. They will farm new players all game, but if you manage to kill them one time, their ego completely explodes. You can tell some of them take it way too personally.
The game itself is good, and I honestly wish I got to play it when everyone was new. But now it feels like the veteran players made it almost impossible for new players to enjoy or stick around.
The game itself is fun but the player base is incredibly toxic and the matchmaking is horrific. It's impossible for new players to do anything but be ganked by veteran players.
Boring game too much of an gap in skill for new players.

Refunded this game after not even 3 hours of playing it. Played this game for the first time back in 2023 after getting it free from epic games. The game was ACTUALLY FUN, and it didnt really have that many sweats. NOW all i saw was people trolling, teaming and being sweats all game long, no respect for any beginners AT ALL. And if you do something the server owners dont like even tho its apart of the game, you get banned. 1 hour of playing deathmatches gave me 3-5 kills and around 50-100 deaths, the sweats are unbelieveable. Only gamemode i found amusing was horde. Otherwise, I DONT recommend this for people who are slow beginners (as in learning the mechanics and skills slow and with time). NOT WORTH 30 EUROS.

Mordhau is one of those games that looks amazing from the outside but feels brutal once you step in. The combat system is deep, skill-based, and clearly rewarding for veterans — but for new players, it’s a wall of pain. The servers are packed with highly skilled players who’ve mastered every feint, drag, and mind game imaginable.

Getting into the game without grinding for hundreds of hours feels nearly impossible. You spend most of your early experience dying repeatedly, often without fully understanding what you did wrong. Instead of a learning curve, it feels more like a learning cliff.

If you enjoy hardcore mastery, patience, and suffering your way toward competence, you might love it. But if you’re looking for casual fun or a smoother onboarding experience, this can quickly become frustrating rather than entertaining.

Mordhau, developed by Triternion, is a multiplayer medieval combat game built around physics-based melee fighting and large battlefield matches.

Combat

The combat system is the game’s defining feature. Players control attack angles, timing, and movement rather than relying on preset animations. Mechanics such as feints, chambers, morphs, and parries create a combat loop that feels closer to a duel than a typical action game.

The learning curve is steep. New players will lose often early on, but the skill ceiling is extremely high.

Game Modes

Main modes include:

Frontline – large objective battles

Invasion – siege-style scenarios

Duel / Deathmatch servers – skill-focused combat

Horde – cooperative survival

Large matches are intentionally chaotic. Siege weapons, cavalry, and dozens of players colliding at once produce unpredictable battles.

Customization

Players build characters using a point-based loadout system that balances weapons, armor weight, and perks. Cosmetic customization is extensive, ranging from realistic knights to intentionally absurd builds.

Overall

Mordhau delivers one of the deepest melee systems in multiplayer gaming. The barrier to entry is high, but players who invest time in learning the mechanics will find a highly rewarding combat experience.

Score: 8.5 / 10

Look. It's a fun game at its core. In a vacuum I would recommend it. But it's not really a game worth getting into anymore due to the low remaining playerbase, many of which are sweatlords.

To get into more detail, the fighting itself is cool. Easy to get into, but hard to master, a large variety of weapons and playstyles. The customization can be done by just grinding the game, but you're not awarded for performance. You're awarded for spending time in the matches. Which arguably is a plus, but it does feel bad to not be rewarded for getting good at the game and letting me speed up customization.

But the problem is the game is almost dead. I'm speaking this as a guy playing on European servers, I would not find games in the morning, only two servers were available in the evenings, roughly 80-120 people. And you'd meet the same people over and over. Many were cool, don't get me wrong, playing around with an unarmored dwarf, or running around half-naked with a pitchfork and so on. Even fellow newbies at times. But there's also a lot of people sweating extremely hard. You'd find a guy with K/D ratio of like 100/20 regularly, using the most unemployed moves on newbies and boasting about it. Again, there are many cool people, but the sweatlords you will meet every time you play leave a sour taste and they're unavoidable.

So as much as I love the game, and you will enjoy it for a while, the frustration of playing against people with 2k hours absolutely stomping you will tire you out.

Mordhau, developed by Triternion, is a multiplayer medieval combat game built around physics-based melee fighting and large battlefield matches.

Combat

The combat system is the game’s defining feature. Players control attack angles, timing, and movement rather than relying on preset animations. Mechanics such as feints, chambers, morphs, and parries create a combat loop that feels closer to a duel than a typical action game.

The learning curve is steep. New players will lose often early on, but the skill ceiling is extremely high.

Game Modes

Main modes include:

Frontline – large objective battles

Invasion – siege-style scenarios

Duel / Deathmatch servers – skill-focused combat

Horde – cooperative survival

Large matches are intentionally chaotic. Siege weapons, cavalry, and dozens of players colliding at once produce unpredictable battles.

Customization

Players build characters using a point-based loadout system that balances weapons, armor weight, and perks. Cosmetic customization is extensive, ranging from realistic knights to intentionally absurd builds.

Overall

Mordhau delivers one of the deepest melee systems in multiplayer gaming. The barrier to entry is high, but players who invest time in learning the mechanics will find a highly rewarding combat experience.

Score: 8.5 / 10

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the player base as consisting mostly of highly skilled, veteran players who dominate newcomers.

citations.review_text:
MORDHAU always felt a step above Chivalry to me. The maps, the sound design, the whole atmosphere, even the combat system, I've always loved it

Easy to pick up but really hard to actually get good at, like a lot of these games. Doesn't matter if it's ranked or just a free for all lobby, you're always having fun, always coming back for another round

The only real downside is running into a very experienced player. At that point they're basically unkillable. There's also a handful of tricks people pull off with certain weapons, feints and movements that feel closer to exploiting a bug than actual skill, and fighting against that is painful

Still, overall it's a good game, you spend a good time bonking heads and just laughing about it

This may be the hardest review I've ever had to write. I love this game. As the "Hours played" can attest, it gave me a lot of happy memories, especially during the stress of the pandemic lockdowns. But I can't in good conscience recommend it to new players as of summer 2026.

Basically, this is and always has been a hard game to get good at--I don't think I ever reached that point--and between new players staying away due to that learning curve, intermediate players falling away from the attrition of time, and both groups being kept away by a lack of updates (I think it's been almost two years since the last update now), the game is left with ghost town servers filled only with the top-tier players. A nice enough bunch, for the most part, but they are SO frustrating to play against because they're just that good.

If you want to take a stab (heh) at the remaining elite-tier players, I wish you luck. I also wish you could have seen this game at its peak. 

Farewell, Mordhau. <Raises blade in one final salute>
hard to get into because most of the playerbase is seasoned vets who will absolutely destroy you but still fun

After 1,400+ hours, I can confidently say that Mordhau is a one-of-a-kind game. I've played plenty of multiplayer games over the years, but none have offered the same level of freedom, expression, and unpredictability that this game does.

The combat system has an incredibly high skill ceiling. Its also one of the biggest hurdles: expect to get destroyed for a long time. This isnt a game where you master the mechanics in a weekend. It takes hundreds of hours before you will even notice your first real improvements, and thousands before you begin to understand the depth of the combat. If youre looking for instant gratification, this probably isnt the game for you. But if you enjoy mastering difficult mechanics, the journey is incredibly rewarding.

One of Mordhaus greatest strengths is how diverse the gameplay can be. You can play as a heavily armored knight, a duelist, an engineer, an archer (JK dont play archer :D), or completely ignore conventional builds and become the guy doing backflips while punching people to death. You run into fist-only acrobats, bow thieves who spend entire matches stealing enemies bows, bards playing music in the middle of a battlefield, roleplayers, trolls, and players who invent completely unique fighting styles. No two matches ever feel exactly the same.

The community deserves its own mention. Yes, it is often toxic. But its also weirdly entertaining. The chat can be absolute chaos, and you can meet some of the funniest, most memorable, and most unhinged people in online gaming. Whether thats a positive or a negative depends on your tolerance for internet culture, but it certainly gives the game personality.

The random moments are what keep me coming back. One second youre locked in an intense duel, the next youre witness a group of players throwing stones at a poor guy, chasing someone with a frying pan, or witnessing an entire frontline collapse because a naked dwarf somehow distracted half the enemy team. The game constantly creat…

Unfortunately, Mordhau is in a rough spot today. The player base is small, and the only players left are absolute sweat lords who have mastered every mechanic, making it pretty brutal for new players.

That being said, when this game was at its peak, it was truly something special. For such a small development team, they created a masterpiece. The massive team battles were absolute chaos, and there was nothing else quite like fighting alongside your brethren in the middle of a full scale medieval battle. Some of my fondest gaming memories came from those moments, fighting side by side with your squad, holding your ground as enemies slowly surrounded you. The combat was satisfying, the battles felt alive, and even things like catapults and archers had their place without ruining the melee focused experience.

Mordhau had so much potential, and it’s sad to see where it ended up. I wouldn’t recommend it to a brand new player today, but I’ll always cherish the years when this game was at its peak.

Peak Mordhau: 10/10
Current Mordhau: 3/10

If the developers ever make a Mordhau 2, I’ll buy it day one.
